summary.qualitative: The candidate is structurally compliant and strong on the mechanical spine of the session: it captures the forward-slash config key discovery, the backup-and-patch, the failed Win+Ctrl+Shift+B attempt, the DisplaySwitch state 4→1 flip, the UAC deny-only diagnosis, the exit-code-1 anomaly, and the Encore build with its check-only smoke test — and its D section consistently labels origins with occasional honest hedging about what is inference. It is materially weaker than the reference on evidence specificity (no GitHub issue numbers, no named web sources, no 'silent stream' behaviour, no 'no supported setting exists' constraint) and on the session's quieter craft signals: the phantom/duplicate MMDevices entries, the single-occurrence regex verification, the visual check of the generated icon, the deliberate no-admin design of Encore, and the knowingly-shipped OneDrive/LOCALAPPDATA shortcut limitation are all missing. Its user-observation section is generic where the reference is sharp — it never credits the user's race-condition hypothesis as correct, never notes the recurrence teaching ('happens from time to time'), and mislabels the user's diagnostic curiosity as a 'growth edge'. Two minor distortions (the turn-3 timing note and the convention-labelled backup) are the only grounding defects; there are no fabrications.
